Warm batter ferments faster than cold batter.

Compare the results of the repeated trials with the hypothesis.
Share the results so that others can check them.

p.title: Discovery of the cell

events.label: Hooke sees cork cells
events.info: Robert Hooke saw box-like compartments in a thin slice of cork and named them cells.

events.label: Leeuwenhoek sees free-living cells
events.info: With better lenses he saw free-living cells in pond water.

events.label: Brown discovers the nucleus
events.info: Robert Brown found the nucleus in plant cells.

events.label: Schleiden: plants are made of cells
events.info: Schleiden proposed that all plants are made of cells.

events.label: Schwann: animals are made of cells
events.info: Schwann extended the cell theory to animals.

events.label: Virchow: cells come from cells
events.info: All cells arise from pre-existing cells.

p.challenge: Put the 6 discoveries that built the cell theory in time order, oldest on top

nodes.info: The nucleus contains chromosomes made of DNA and controls the cell's activities.

nodes.text: Ribosomes on rough ER make protein
nodes.info: Ribosomes make proteins. Rough ER has ribosomes on it.
The endoplasmic reticulum is a network of channels that carries materials through the cell.
The Golgi apparatus packages materials and sends them to where they are needed.

nodes.text: Sent out through the cell membrane
nodes.info: The selectively permeable membrane lets some substances in and out.

nodes.info: Nervous tissue: neurons carry the message as nerve impulses.
A neuron has a cell body, short branched dendrites and a long axon.
Muscular tissue contracts to cause movement. Leg muscles are voluntary.
Tendons are connective tissue that join muscle to bone.

nodes.text: Bones move; ligaments hold the joint
nodes.info: Ligaments join bone to bone at a joint.
Nerve, muscle and connective tissue worked together.

p.title: The drooping plant on a hot day

panels.t: Hot day: leaves lose water vapour through stomata.
Water is lost faster than xylem can bring it up.
Leaf cells lose water and the leaves droop.
Evening: the plant is watered; roots absorb water.
Xylem carries the water up to the leaves.
Cells fill with water, become firm; leaves stand up.

Each square is 1 km. Plot a point exactly 5 km (displacement) from Home. Tip: 3 km east then 4 km north is a 7 km walk, but only 5 km of displacement!
A car starts from rest and reaches 72 km/h (= 20 m/s) in 10 s. Set u and a so your graphs match the dashed ones. Use a = (v − u) ÷ t.
p.winText: u = 0 and a = (20 − 0) ÷ 10 = 2 m/s². The speed–time graph is a straight sloping line: uniform acceleration.

p.challenge: A car moving at 20 m/s brakes with a = −4 m/s². Predict the stopping distance with v² = u² + 2as, then set u and a and press Go to check: it should stop after 50 m.
p.winText: 0 = 20² + 2 × (−4) × s, so s = 400 ÷ 8 = 50 m. The car stops after 5 s (v = u + at).

p.title: Iron + sulphur: mixture or compound?

panels.t: Iron filings and sulphur powder are mixed.
A magnet pulls the iron out: it keeps its properties.
The teacher heats part of the mixture strongly.
They combine chemically: new compound, iron sulphide.
The magnet cannot pull iron out of the compound.

Balanced forces cannot move the 50 kg almirah. Find the smallest push that makes the force unbalanced, so it starts to move.
p.winText: Your push just beat the friction: the net force is no longer zero, so the almirah starts moving (first law).

p.challenge: Mass is a measure of inertia. Keep the push at 60 N and change the mass: which load speeds up at only 2 m/s²? (a = F ÷ m)
p.winText: A heavier load has more inertia, so the same push gives it less acceleration: 60 N ÷ 30 kg = 2 m/s².

events.label: Rutherford's nuclear model

events.label: Bohr's model: fixed shells

Step from carbon (6) through the elements to magnesium (12) and argon (18). Count the outer-shell electrons: Mg (2, 8, 2) has valency 2.

A water molecule (H₂O) has a mass of 18 u. Each hydrogen atom is 1 u. Each box x is one oxygen atom. Find its mass.
p.winText: x = 16 u, so an oxygen atom is 16 times as heavy as a hydrogen atom. Check: H₂O = 2 × 1 + 16 = 18 u.

nodes.info: The outer ear gathers sound and sends it into the ear canal.
The auditory canal leads to the eardrum.
The tympanic membrane vibrates with the sound.

nodes.text: Hammer, anvil, stirrup pass it on
nodes.info: Three tiny bones amplify the vibrations. The stirrup is the smallest bone in the body.
The snail-shaped cochlea in the inner ear turns vibrations into signals.
The brain interprets the signals as sound.

p.title: Budding in Hydra

panels.t: A small outgrowth (bud) forms on the parent Hydra.
The bud grows bigger while still attached.
It develops into a tiny new Hydra.
It separates and lives on its own, like its parent.
A potato kept in the dark sprouts shoots from its eyes.
A piece of potato with an eye is cut out.
The piece is planted in moist soil.
It grows into a new potato plant, with no seeds.
Bread mould (Rhizopus) makes spores in sporangia.
Sporangia burst; spores spread through the air.
A spore lands on moist, warm bread.
It grows into a new mould.

nodes.text: Male gamete fuses with the egg

The ovule becomes the seed.
The petals and stamens usually wither and fall.

p.title: Life cycle of a frog

panels.t: Hundreds of eggs are laid in water.
Sperm fertilise the eggs outside the body.
Each zygote divides again and again: an embryo.
A tadpole with a tail hatches and swims.
Metamorphosis: the tadpole becomes an adult frog.

nodes.info: No nuclear membrane, no membrane-bound organelles.
The organism is eukaryotic. Is it a single cell?

nodes.text: Do its cells have a cell wall?
nodes.info: Many-celled eukaryote. Look for a cell wall.

nodes.text: Does it have chlorophyll and make its own food?
nodes.info: Autotroph or heterotroph?
Multicellular autotrophs with cellulose cell walls, e.g. lotus.
Heterotrophs that absorb food from dead matter; chitin cell walls, e.g. mushroom.
Multicellular heterotrophs with no cell wall, e.g. tiger.
Unicellular eukaryotes, e.g. Amoeba, Paramecium, Euglena.
Prokaryotic and unicellular, e.g. bacteria in curd.

nodes.info: Trees and the animals living in them are lost.

nodes.text: No roots to hold the soil
nodes.info: Roots normally bind the soil of the lithosphere.
Heavy rain carries the loose soil down the slope.
The washed-away soil makes rivers muddy and can cause floods downstream.
Fewer trees take in carbon dioxide.

p.title: The nitrogen cycle

panels.t: Plants cannot use nitrogen gas from the air directly.
Lightning and Rhizobium (in legume roots) fix nitrogen.
Nitrifying bacteria make nitrates in the soil.
Plants absorb nitrates to make proteins.
Denitrifying bacteria return nitrogen gas to the air.

p.title: Why climates differ

places.name: Shimla
places.info: High altitude: temperature falls with height, so Shimla stays cool even in May.

places.name: Delhi
places.info: Far from the sea: very hot summers and cold winters (extreme climate).

places.name: Mumbai
places.info: On the coast: the Arabian Sea keeps temperatures moderate all year.
